question: What is another common clinical name for synovial fluid aspiration?
explanation: Arthrocentesis is the formal medical term for inserting a needle into a joint space to withdraw fluid. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T8#GNS222_U1_T8_h1)

question: Why is synovial fluid aspiration performed for joint swelling?

options.A: To permanently stop fluid production in the joint
options.B: To deliver oral anti-inflammatory drugs directly
options.C: To diagnose the cause and relieve pressure
options.D: To replace natural fluid with synthetic blood

explanation: Draining the joint reduces painful pressure and provides a sample to test for infection or crystals. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T8#GNS222_U1_T8_h1)

question: The main contraindication for performing an arthrocentesis is what condition?

options.D: Skin infection over the puncture site

explanation: Inserting a needle through infected skin can introduce bacteria directly into the sterile joint space, causing septic arthritis. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T8#GNS222_U1_T8_h2)

question: A patient on active anticoagulant therapy requires a joint aspiration. What is the primary risk?
explanation: Anticoagulants impair clotting, raising the danger of bleeding inside the closed joint space during needle entry. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T8#GNS222_U1_T8_h2)

question: What medication class must the nurse specifically check for before a joint aspiration?
explanation: Anticoagulants increase bleeding risks and must be identified prior to invasive needle procedures. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T8#GNS222_U1_T8_h3)

question: A client scheduled for knee arthrocentesis has a fresh skin scrape over the patella. What action should the nurse take?

options.A: Apply a strong antiseptic cream and send the patient immediately
options.B: Cover the scrape with waterproof tape and begin the procedure
options.C: Proceed with the aspiration since surface scrapes do not matter
options.D: Notify the doctor because skin breaks contraindicate the puncture site

explanation: Compromised skin over the intended insertion path poses an infection risk and usually requires rescheduling or site adjustment. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T8#GNS222_U1_T8_h3)

question: Why is local anesthetic without epinephrine used for joint aspiration?

options.A: To prevent vasoconstriction around the joint tissues
options.B: To add color and visibility to the fluid sample
options.C: To speed up the numbing effect of the medicine
options.D: To neutralize any bacteria present in the skin

explanation: Epinephrine causes vasoconstriction, which can reduce blood supply to the local tissue area around joints. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T8#GNS222_U1_T8_h4)

question: What is the primary role of the nurse during the arthrocentesis procedure?

options.B: Maintain the sterile field and handle specimens
options.C: Insert the needle directly into the joint capsule
options.D: Perform the microscopic analysis of the fluid

explanation: The nurse supports the clinician by keeping the field sterile, comforting the client, and labeling collected samples correctly. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T8#GNS222_U1_T8_h4)

question: What appearance is most characteristic of normal, healthy synovial fluid?
explanation: Healthy synovial fluid is transparent and has a pale straw or yellow coloration. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T8#GNS222_U1_T8_h5)

question: A synovial fluid white blood cell count above 50,000 cells/uL strongly points to what condition?
explanation: Extremely high white blood cell counts in joint fluid indicate an active bacterial infection requiring urgent treatment. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T8#GNS222_U1_T8_h5)

question: What post-procedural instruction should the nurse give regarding the aspirated joint?

options.A: Perform heavy exercises to test the joint
options.B: Remove the pressure dressing right away
options.C: Rest the joint for twenty-four hours
options.D: Immerse the joint in warm water immediately

explanation: Resting the joint prevents irritation and bleeding at the puncture site following needle insertion. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T8#GNS222_U1_T8_h6)

question: Which symptom reported by a client days after arthrocentesis requires immediate medical attention?

options.A: A small bruise on the skin surface
options.B: Mild soreness around the needle site

explanation: Fever and spreading warmth suggest a developing joint infection that needs prompt medical evaluation. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T8#GNS222_U1_T8_h6)
